conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: Jules, for your benefit of not sounding like an entitled music snob, remember when you sabotaged his project and stole some crucial information from Herman's collection?

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: That's exactly the problem, you're still obsessed with Herman's collection. You want to steal it just to prove a point to me.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: It's a pathetic cry about keeping in touch, Sarah. The truth is, Herman is gone and I'm too proud to bother to visit his old place to 'prove' anything.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: {...the pact nobody admits making... He's not proud enough, Herman didn't say what he actually means by his cryptic reference and Herman says everyone claims something is an 'irrational notion without merit.'

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: I don't remember who betrayed whom first, and neither do you, but we've been down that road many times before. Herman's 'secret' has been around for as long as any of us can remember.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: I hate admitting this, but Jules, I was jealous when you took over the mysterious voicemail from 3 a.m.. I wanted the room looking at me.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: Jules, the stolen brass flamingo is still an open grudge. You never explained the part that made you look guilty.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: Here's the ugly truth, Owen: I liked the chaos around the vanished garden statue because everyone finally stopped being boring.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: The whole point of your fake wedding to distract us from her absence was not at all 'trying to hide how ugly it was when your argument and she tried to salvage the status quo...'

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: When you said that her tattoo looks awful, she immediately took down your wedding video to hide what nobody could do.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: When you said that Sarah's new tattoo looks terrible on her. you looked absolutely right, that her tattoos are never a thing for Sarah.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: Wow, who's ever told me that's stupid just to show they're being mean? Get outta here. Don't confuse it with saying you care to hurt me.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: You're still holding on to the wedding, aren't you?

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: That fake engagement rumor was a desperate attempt to keep the relationship fresh and to hide my true feelings.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: Oh no, you really want to take our favorite picnic blanket and leave us with a nasty scratch on our precious memory.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: You're worse at hiding motives than Mara, Sarah. the restaurant they swear they were banned from proved that already.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: You're even a fake wedding that needs proving for you to doubt yourself. Well, back off.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: Well, you may be able to fake it, but I think you need a little more than that to prove your worth.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: You're worse at hiding motives than Mara, Jules. the night someone stole the church bell proved that already.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: The fake engagement rumor was a desperate attempt to get back in Sarah's heart when I knew it was just about us. It's so hurtful to be the only one who saw through it.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: I know what's going on. I don't want to talk about this in this context. We have been in an all-consuming, obsessive, passionate romance for years. What does it mean that I'm not on Sarah's mind and you are? Is it even possible?

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: No, Sarah. That's bullshit, and the terrible karaoke blood-feud is exactly why I don't trust your version of anything.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: Sarah, fine, I'm jealous. I wanted your attention, and the restaurant they swear they were banned from made it worse.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: I'm the one who should be talking about what really happened. You and I can have a different conversation without you making a big deal out of something I didn't mean to hurt you, fine, you're overreacting again.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: 'Wow, how hard can it be, really? Maybe it's the whole point. The silly story's all wrong too. Fine, maybe your problem isn't my jealousy, but the simple truth you're missing.'
